$comment: Concrete cost of each classical -> post-quantum swap. Byte sizes are from the FIPS standards themselves; a migration plan that ignores them under-budgets bandwidth, certificate stores and embedded flash.

sources.FIPS 203: Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard, NIST, Aug 2024
sources.FIPS 204: Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard, NIST, Aug 2024
sources.FIPS 205: Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Standard, NIST, Aug 2024

sources.RFC 9954: Hybrid key exchange framework for TLS 1.3

algorithm_sizes_bytes.$comment: public_key / private_key / signature or ciphertext, in bytes.

recommendations.$comment: Keyed by algorithm family. 'hybrid' is the RFC 10024 option where a TLS handshake is involved.

signature.rationale: Lattice signature at NIST level 3; the general-purpose replacement.

key-agree.rationale: ML-KEM-768 at NIST level 3; deploy hybrid first per RFC 10024 so a lattice break does not regress security.

pke.rationale: RSA key transport has no direct PQ analogue; restructure to a KEM.

signature.alternative_rationale: Prefer SLH-DSA for firmware and root-of-trust signing: conservative hash-based security, tiny public key, at the cost of a 7856 B signature.

signature.rationale: DSA is already deprecated classically; migrate directly to ML-DSA.

block-cipher.rationale: Grover halves the effective key length. AES-128 drops to 64-bit quantum security; AES-256 retains 128.
Already disallowed by NIST SP 800-131A Rev.2 after 2023, quantum considerations aside.

stream-cipher.rationale: RC4 is prohibited in TLS by RFC 7465.

hash.rationale: Classically broken; not a quantum issue.
Classically broken; not a quantum issue.

latency_notes.$comment: Order-of-magnitude guidance only. Q-DARPAN reports byte deltas as measured facts and latency as a qualitative note, because handshake latency depends on the operator's network, not on the algorithm alone.
latency_notes.ML-KEM-768: Keygen and encapsulation are faster than X25519 in most software stacks; the cost is bytes on the wire, not CPU.
latency_notes.ML-DSA-65: Signing and verification are competitive with ECDSA; the cost is the 3309 B signature.
latency_notes.SLH-DSA-128s: Signing is orders of magnitude slower than ECDSA. Acceptable for firmware signed once, not for per-connection use.
latency_notes.X25519MLKEM768: Adds roughly 1.1 kB to the TLS ClientHello and the same to the server response, which can push the ClientHello past a single MTU.
